static_traits.name: Tan Haili
static_traits.educational_background: Bachelor's degree in political science from a state university; currently a graduate student in law school
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to talk with, but has not shared the feelings of inferiority with them; interactions with classmates are affected by lack of confidence
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological problems; no psychotherapy history; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic; emotions inclined toward anxiety, frequent self-doubt and belittling of own achievements; able to cooperate in exploration and willing to change; neutral tone

basic_info.main_problem: Because my undergraduate school was not prestigious enough, after entering law school I began to feel not good enough and doubt my abilities; comparison and pressure make me frequently think 'I don't belong here / I'm not as good as them' in class and study groups, affecting my confidence, study motivation, academic performance, social interaction, and sleep.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this sense of inferiority markedly affects my academic performance and overall physical and mental health.
growth_experiences: In the first semester of graduate school, Tan Haili found that many classmates had graduated from Ivy League and other famous schools, producing a strong sense of falling behind and the thought 'I do not belong here'; afterward, she frequently engaged in social comparison in class and study groups, gradually forming a cycle of inferiority and doubting her abilities, accompanied by disturbed sleep and declined self-care.

After completing a bachelor's degree in political science at a state university, she was successfully admitted to law school; during law school, she received positive feedback from professors on several assignments, but she often attributed these achievements to luck or politeness.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / not as good as my peers
My worth depends on my prestigious-school background

special_situations.event: Studying and interacting with classmates from prestigious schools in class or study groups
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my undergraduate institution is not a 'prestigious school' enough, it means I am inherently inferior to them and I do not belong here
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces speaking and participation, keeping a low presence in study groups to avoid being compared
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are smarter and more capable than me; I do not belong here

special_situations.event: The professor gives positive feedback or praises assignment performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only perfect and absolutely objective results count; verbal praise may just be politeness; praise for a non-famous-school background is not credible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Discounting positive evidence, repeatedly seeking more reassurance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is just luck, or the teacher is just being polite

special_situations.event: At night, recalls comparisons with classmates and worries about whether they can 'meet their standards' in the future
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach a level comparable to peers from prestigious schools, I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated thinking and worry, trying to control unease through over-preparation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I cannot do as well as them, I am worthless

special_situations.event: Talking about undergraduate background and resume in group discussions or peer exchanges
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: In comparisons, prioritizing focusing on one's shortcomings to avoid complacency and criticism
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses on background 'disadvantages', ignoring achievements made and evidence of ability
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My undergraduate degree is too ordinary; this shows my ability is also average

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and accepted, becoming a 'qualified' member of the group
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being belittled and excluded in comparisons, experiencing shame and loss of worth
defense_goal: Reduces being judged by lowering exposure and avoiding speaking up
Explaining worth with rational standards such as school prestige to gain a sense of control
Temporarily relieving anxiety by seeking reassurance from others

object_relations.self_representation: An outsider who is not qualified and needs to prove oneself
object_relations.object_representation: Superior and picky judges (classmates/the outside world)

object_relations.self_representation: A student still uneasy after being affirmed
object_relations.object_representation: A well-meaning but not entirely reliable comforter (professor/authority figure)
object_relations.linking_affect: Doubt, brief relief, then unease again

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor points to her strengths or invites her to acknowledge positive evidence (such as being admitted to law school and praised by professors)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Suspicion toward positive evidence: this might be politeness / chance, not enough to prove I am good enough
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintains a restrained and polite tone, uses expressions such as 'probably just luck / the teacher was being polite' to downplay achievements, and raises more detailed demands to weaken affirmation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor explores the emotional sources of comparison and shame, inviting them to stay with present feelings
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Directly touching shame would spiral out of control or feel worse, so it needs to be discussed using 'objective standards'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Answers in factual, abstract language about academics, rankings, and school tiers, with a calm tone, avoiding emotional vocabulary, and shifting away from present feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor affirms a specific success and invites them to internalize the feeling of 'I am worthy'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Acknowledging worth brings the risk of being seen and compared again
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds with brief negations or questioning expressions (such as 'that does not count' and 'just a coincidence'), in a flat tone, quickly moving to the next topic.

manifestations: After entering law school, frequently feels 'I do not belong here', withdrawing in class and study groups
Strictly ties self-worth to prestigious-school standards, making it hard to build equal and genuine connections with peers
outcomes: Decreased learning motivation and aggravated self-doubt

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Regards a famous-school background as the absolute standard for measuring personal value, forming the inner rule that 'one must reach the famous-school level of peers to count as qualified'
Replacing self-evaluation with external prestige, difficulty receiving positive feedback

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Overly cautious in class and group discussions, limits own speaking for fear of exposing 'insufficient ability'
Repeatedly nitpicks one's own achievements; hard to internalize their value

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language manifestations include: 'Forget it, I will just endure it', 'I should not trouble others', and so on
manifestations: When they should express opinions or ask questions, instead suppresses the self, reducing participation to avoid being judged
Internalizes anxiety about comparison into self-blame and insomnia

exception_events.target_problem: In classroom or study-task situations, Tan Haili usually avoids expressing herself due to self-doubt, with reduced motivation, which in turn affects academic performance and confidence
exception_events.unique_outcome: In several course assignments, the client achieved good grades and received positive feedback from professors; unlike the usual self-negation, these results objectively showed a relatively high level of ability
exception_events.reason: Clues: persistent investment and diligence, analytical ability; support from professor feedback - these conditions contributed to better performance

positive_force: A diligent and persistently engaged learning attitude
Having some analytical and critical-thinking ability
Has been admitted to law school; has an objective foundation of academic ability
Willing to try joining a study group and seeking help
negative_force: Self-deprecation caused by excessive social comparison
Depending on external validation, difficulty internalizing positive feedback
Disqualifying positive evidence and all-or-nothing thinking maintain beliefs of inferiority
Anxiety and sleep disturbance weaken daytime functioning and study efficiency
Withdrawal and avoidance in group situations reduce opportunities for practice and positive feedback

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding speaking and participating in class and study groups
antecedent: Studying/discussing together with classmates from prestigious schools
Being called on or needing to express opinions in a group
target_behavior.core_reason: Ties self-worth to the institution's fame, fearing exposure of 'insufficient ability' in comparisons and experiencing shame
target_behavior.function: Escaping judgment and shame, reducing anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Reducing opportunities for practice and positive feedback, further weakening confidence and academic performance

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly seeks reassurance from the professor or others (Reassurance seeking)
antecedent: Still feeling uneasy after receiving assignment grades or feedback
Approaching exams or facing high-load courses
target_behavior.core_reason: Relying on external validation to confirm self-worth, difficulty internalizing positive information
target_behavior.function: Gaining short-term soothing to relieve anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Strengthens dependence on external approval and maintains self-doubt long-term

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly worrying before sleep about 'whether I can meet peer standards', leading to difficulty falling asleep
antecedent: At night, reviewing the day's comparisons and classroom performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Excessive worry under all-or-nothing and catastrophizing tendencies, attempting to control uncertainty through thinking
target_behavior.function: Gaining a surface sense of control by rehearsing worst-case scenarios
target_behavior.consequence: Disturbed sleep, decreased daytime attention and energy, further affecting study and emotions
